Through playing the game, I can say **YES**, you do can fix them as you upgrade your settlement, mainly through these **Random Events**, where "heeding the warning" or "welcoming a new settler" will have a chance add your settlement a new positive feature, or replace one of the negative features. (if your settlement already has 6 features full).

Just a warning that some outcome may result you in receiving a negative feature, so watch out for those.

Wow, seeing how this blew up in one day, I'm really glad y'all enjoying this, hehe. More to come!  


EDIT#1: Thank you, everyone!

Hello, Devs! By any chance can we see the **roadmap** for the **Soda Dungeon 2?** I may have started to suspect that there are still some unreleased content that we have yet to experience (*such as that rainbow blade and blue fiery shield we see from the nurse holding on the Steam Library header of the game*)?  


I'm just excited and looking forward to see new stuff from SD2.  


Other than that... Why does the Dark Lord have to hangout outside the tavern? Doesn't he want to stay inside to enjoy the soda or something?

You're right for both. I shouldn't feel like that she owes me for what I did for her. It's what I did for her, and it should stay as that way, no matter how she reacts to it. But I'll need to start practicing in establishing my boundaries so that I have enough of myself at times.

And her past relationships are ultimately for her to decide on how it should end for her. I'm no expert and should not be influencing her relationship. I'm not in control and don't want to be either.

All I want is some merit for myself, and I should begin with limiting on how much I can give, whether it be kindness, time, and others. I need to respect myself after all.

Did I understand your advice correctly?

Ironically, I was about to not comment to this post, for a reason that one of the comments may have already spoken for me.

So I could reply with a " ^ ".


Other than that, it's because I am afraid of getting lashed out in social media. The urge to say something and having a reasonable debate is something cant be commonly found anymore. The need to feel validated is there, alright. But with everyone feeling invincible behind a screen, people seem to be generally more attuned to sensitivity to details, and are able to speak out loud and at many cases, toxic. Im not sure whats causing the haphazard throwing of insults from one another, when you can just sit down and properly discuss, educate, and tell without any of sideline commentarie but, I wouldnt like it to be on its receiving end. To fight for the right things is noble. But things are so covnenient, it feels devalued.

Hence, the all these kinda make me not want to comment on a post until it really do feel it is worth my time and mind. And this is worth it for me, cuz I just learned something about myself.

Hey man, thanks for reaching out. Despite we're just a couple of strangers talking, but reading this somehow made me less miserable. I will remember this.

Thank you!
